overviewParagraphs: Phokeethra Country Club carries the prestigious distinction of having hosted the Asian Tour's Cambodian Open — an accolade that certifies the course to a professional tournament standard and makes it one of the most credentialled layouts in Cambodia. The Asian Tour brings the world's top emerging professionals together for a serious championship test, and Phokeethra met that standard convincingly during its time as the national Open host.

The course's signature challenge is its system of forced water carries — genuine carry requirements off tees and into greens that leave no room for the layup approach that more forgiving designs allow. The water is positioned to punish truly errant shots decisively while still rewarding conservative but accurate target-finding. It is a more demanding playing experience than either Angkor Golf Resort or the Chhun On courses, and is best suited to golfers who want a genuine championship test alongside their Siem Reap cultural itinerary.

AGS recommends Phokeethra as a strong option for lower-handicap discerning golfers visiting Siem Reap who want to experience the course where professional golf was played in Cambodia. Pairing it with Angkor Golf Resort creates an excellent two-round Siem Reap program at contrasting levels of celebrity design prestige.

curatorBriefHtml: Phokeethra Country Club is a premier Par 72 championship layout in Siem Reap, Cambodia, crafted by Weerayudth Phetbuasak (2004) and stretching to 6,791 Yards (Blue Tees) across a tropical, near angkor temples environment. In Asia Golf Specialists' (AGS) field evaluations, the course stands out for its 11th-century angkor bridge historic feature (Cross historic bridge on 9) and natural lagoons & palm corridors (Classic tropical parkland).

From an itinerary-engineering perspective, Phokeethra Country Club (Resort & Visitor Access via AGS) requires advance flight allocation and experienced local caddie pairing—particularly during the peak Cambodia dry season. Our curatorial scorecard specifically notes its caddie local line knowledge (Warm, experienced caddies), making pre-reserved morning tee times and private door-to-clubhouse VIP transfers essential for maintaining pace of play.

When integrated into a multi-round Siem Reap golf tour by AGS, Phokeethra Country Club provides a distinct architectural test by Weerayudth Phetbuasak that complements neighboring regional layouts while keeping daily hotel-to-tee transfer times streamlined.

scorecard.verdict: Home of the Asian Tour's Johnnie Walker Cambodian Open. Features an authentic 11th-century stone bridge on the 9th hole and delivers a classic parkland challenge amidst ancient history.

faqs.q: What are the key course specifications for Phokeethra Country Club?
faqs.a: Phokeethra Country Club in Siem Reap, Cambodia is a Par 72 championship layout designed by Weerayudth Phetbuasak (opened 2004), measuring 6,791 Yards (Blue Tees) within a tropical, near angkor temples setting. It is particularly noted for 11th-century angkor bridge historic feature (Cross historic bridge on 9).

faqs.q: How do I secure tee times and caddies at Phokeethra Country Club?
faqs.a: Phokeethra Country Club operates under resort & visitor access via ags protocols. Asia Golf Specialists secures guaranteed morning tee times, compulsory caddie and cart pairings (caddie local line knowledge (Warm, experienced caddies)), and private VIP transfers from your Siem Reap hotel as part of a custom golf itinerary.

faqs.q: What playing conditions and turf can golfers expect at Phokeethra Country Club?
faqs.a: Our field inspection highlights Phokeethra Country Club's natural lagoons & palm corridors (Classic tropical parkland) alongside 11th-century angkor bridge historic feature (Cross historic bridge on 9). Standard championship golf attire (collared shirts, tailored trousers or shorts, and soft-spike golf shoes) is strictly enforced by the starter.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to play Phokeethra Country Club?
faqs.a: November through May is the recommended season for Phokeethra Country Club Siem Reap.
